description:
The pkix-lint crate contains four separate hex encode/decode implementations:

1. lib.rs serde_helpers::cert_sha256_hex — uses `char::from_digit` + push (allocation-light).
2. deviation.rs hex_encode (line 537) — uses `format!("{:02x}", b)` in a loop with push_str (per-byte heap allocation).
3. oscal/emit.rs hex (line 822) + hex_digit (line 831) — hand-rolled with explicit ASCII offset math.
4. oscal/parse.rs hex_decode (line 824) + nibble (line 840) — the only decoder.

Four implementations of essentially the same algorithm is a maintenance drift risk: the lib.rs serde helper enforces lowercase, deviation.rs enforces lowercase via format!, emit.rs enforces lowercase explicitly, and parse.rs accepts mixed case. If any rule changes (e.g., a future canonical hex spec requires uppercase, or strips/inserts separators), four spots need updating. 

Idiomatic Rust: either (a) add a small `hex` crate-private module exposing `encode_lower(bytes: &[u8]) -> String` and `decode(s: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, _>` and have all four sites use it, or (b) pull in the well-known `hex` crate dependency (already MIT-licensed, zero-dep itself, used widely in RustCrypto). Option (a) keeps the dep tree light; option (b) follows the workspace convention of preferring published crates over hand-rolled cryptography-adjacent utilities. Either way, deviation.rs's per-byte format!-based encoder is the worst of the four (heap allocation per byte) and should be replaced regardless.
title: Hex encode/decode logic duplicated four times across the crate
